exchanges: Okay so todays build day was long but we got the whole roof sheathed on the house on maple which honestly I didnt think we would
That's a big milestone. Getting the roof on is a real turning point for a build.
Ya ahmed was so happy, hes our foreman, he kept saying ahead of schedule ahead of schedule over and over lol
Hard not to be thrilled when a volunteer build is ahead of schedule.
he knows his stuff though, he was an architect for like 35 years before he retired so he spots every mistake from across the yard
That kind of experience must make him a great foreman to learn from.
totally. we also have the twins, grace and gloria, they're in their fifties and they can outwork any of the young guys
That's impressive. Do they always volunteer together?
always, they carpool from the east end. grace plays rugby in an over 40s league which explains a lot about how she swings a hammer
That makes sense. Players in that sport tend to be tough.
and gloria does curling, which she says is way harder than it looks, I'll take her word for it
It's deceptively tough. All that sweeping is a workout.
siobhan wasnt there today which was weird, shes never missed one
Hope everything's okay with her.
ya so turns out she's on crutches, broke her ankle dancing at her daughters wedding on saturday, of all things
What a way to get hurt. At least it comes with a good story.
she texted the group chat a pic of her cast covered in wedding guest signatures lol
That's a great souvenir, even if a painful one.
viktor brought a giant pot of borscht for lunch which was perfect because it was freezing
Hot soup on a cold build site sounds ideal.
he makes it every build day in winter, its his grandmothers recipe from kyiv
Family recipes are the best kind of build-site fuel.
the family who's moving in came by too, lakshmi and her two kids. she cried when she saw the roof
That must have been a moving moment for everyone.
it was, honestly I teared up too. she works as a nurse at the general and she's been on the waitlist for three years
Three years is a long wait. It must feel unreal to see it coming together.
kofi is our youngest, hes 18 and starting at george brown for carpentry in the fall, ahmed basically adopted him
That's a great mentorship. He'll learn a lot from someone that experienced.
ahmed even gave him his old tool belt which was very sweet
That's a meaningful gesture. Kofi will probably treasure it.
ok wait I have to fix something, ahmed wasnt an architect, he was a surveyor. he told me that at lunch and I mixed it up already
Fair enough, both are people who know a building site well.
he said architects draw pretty pictures and surveyors tell them where the ground actually is lol
That sounds like a joke he's told many times.
next build day is saturday, were starting the windows
Windows will make it look like a real house. Are you on that crew?
Ya me and grace and gloria. Siobhan wants to come and sit in a lawn chair and supervise lol
That sounds like the perfect job for someone on crutches.
my shoulders are so sore from holding sheathing over my head
Overhead work is brutal on shoulders. Some gentle stretching and a hot shower should help.
ill try. any stretch you recommend
A doorway stretch is good: forearms on the door frame, then step forward gently until you feel it across your chest and the front of your shoulders.
ok that helped a little already
Good. Do it a few times tonight and again in the morning.
oh also a new volunteer started today, his name is dmitri, hes a plumber so ahmed was thrilled, we never get plumbers
A skilled tradesperson on a volunteer build is gold. That'll save a lot of headaches later.
he said he'll do all the rough-in for free on his days off
That's incredibly generous. Volunteers like that make a huge difference.
this crew is honestly the best part of my week
It sounds like a really special group to be part of.

ahmed was an architect before he retired right
what does viktor do for work
dmitri seems like hes gonna fit right in
